question_verdicts.reason: It is the page's P1 ask (Research.md:283: 'The lowest voltage at the display is not stated, and P1 asks'). No page gives it. One clause of the why is false. The tree names the display board as the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7 Rev1.2 (firmware/panel/components/board/include/board_pins.h:2 and :138) and cites its schematic outside the tree. It gives no input range for the board. The why should read 'The tree names the board and gives no input range for it.'

It is the page's P1 ask (Research.md:283; IOBoard.md:386). docs/Link.md:19-23 names the native USB and a second USB-C socket behind the USB-UART bridge. The tree does not describe the board's power path, and board_pins.h:138-139 states that its schematic 'was never traced'.

The value needs a question: it is an assumption (marking 12). The condition, however, leaves out the IO board running from the DC input. Research.md:283 states the blocking without a condition: 'a display powered from its own USB-C at the same time feeds nothing back into the IO board'. A host's VBUS faces the IO board's 5 V rail through the cable in that state too. An added question asks it for every state.

F6 (Research.md:534) gives 5 V with no tolerance. A setpoint raised to cover the drop at 2 A (Research.md:283) reaches the display at light load, so the display's highest input voltage bounds the setpoint. No page states it.

IOBoard.md:334-336 give the voltage and current but no fault behaviour for a supply that leaves the board on the link cable. busfault_screen.c:159 and :217 name a connector only nearly seated as a fault. The limit decides between an ideal diode and a current-limiting switch.
IOBoard.md:332 states that overvoltage protection exists and gives no withstand voltage. No other page does either. The TPS25947 seed's Vabsmax_cont of 28 V was re-read at 2026-09-28T10:33:19Z.

IOBoard.md:332 and :374 state that the threshold is not stated. The TPS55285's 22 V (re-read 2026-09-28T10:33:18Z) bounds it from above. Neither Research.md:61 nor STATUS.md:25 says whether 20 V includes the source's tolerance.
Neither IOBoard.md:331-333 nor the R5 row gives a transient level for the board input. R3's transients are on the ESC pack path only (Research.md:281, IOBoard.md:385).
IOBoard.md:331-333 put each protection 'on the board's power input', and IOBoard.md:322-323 define two inputs. The R5 row lists the protections without naming an input.
IOBoard.md:333 and :374 state that the inrush limit is not stated.
IOBoard.md:374 lists the lowest input voltage the board runs from as not known. 'Present' in IOBoard.md:324 and Research.md:61 carries no voltage.
IOBoard.md:322-338 give no interruption limit. docs/Safety.md:26-30 lists a brown-out among the causes that stop the edges, so a display dropout at switchover opens every gate.

It carries the assumption at marking 7. Power.md:68 gives no source and covers the DC input only, and IOBoard.md:326 states that the efficiency from the pack is not stated. The TPS55285's 8 A typical switch current limit (re-read 2026-09-28T10:33:18Z) is under 9.9 A, so R6's check may cap option 2. The figure R5 sizes for is still the owner's to set or to mark for research.
IOBoard.md:384 states that it is not known and assigns it to R5. A yes adds a third source to the selection.
It carries the assumption at marking 3. No owner answer gives the 2S pack's charge voltage: F9 gives the floor, S9 the makers and F8 the charge current.
IOBoard.md:330 states that the reconnect condition is not stated, and F9's answer (Research.md:537) sets the floor only.
It carries the assumption at marking 6. IOBoard.md:328 states that the hysteresis width is not stated.

F9 (Research.md:537) gives 3.0 V with no tolerance, and does not say whether it is a nominal or a lowest trip point. 0 to 50 °C is the only temperature range the tree gives for the board (Monostable.md:27).
Neither F9 nor IOBoard.md:327-330 gives a filter time. Without a delay, a load step of about 9.9 A on the pack can briefly pull a cell's terminal voltage under 3.0 V and trip the disconnect.
The tree states no current limit for a disconnected pack. A pack left at 3.0 V a cell keeps discharging through whatever monitors it.

Research.md:61 says only 'in hardware'. R5 (Research.md:283) holds the disconnect and R7 (Research.md:285) the pack's protection, and both run in T3 (Research.md:337). Whether a threshold written by firmware counts as 'in hardware' is for the owner to say, since it is his decision.
Research.md:283 has R5 size the rails without the R6 to R8 parts, and P5 returns an overrun as a conflict. No margin is stated.
IOBoard.md:338 lists the loads with no accuracy. F3 and F4 give 5 V with no tolerance.

IOBoard.md:338 states that the excitation current is not stated. F3 (Research.md:531) gives the channels and 5 V only. The load cells are external sensors, and R13's seeds are ADCs (Research.md:291), so this is not a supply current from T4.
IOBoard.md:387 states that the encoder's current is not stated, and F4 (Research.md:532) gives none. The encoder is the operator's device, not a part from T2 or T4.
F4 (Research.md:532) gives 12 V with no tolerance.

The R5 row covers the receiver's supply 'if the board powers one', and IOBoard.md:287 lists whether it does as not known. docs/Receivers.md:15-16 names signal and ground only, and docs/Receivers.md:29 names receiver power as a cause of a silent bus.

added.question: Does the link cable's supply block current from the display back into the IO board whenever the display is on its own USB-C, in every state of the IO board (unpowered, running from the 2S pack, running from the DC input): yes or no?
added.why: Research.md:283 and IOBoard.md:386 state the blocking with no condition and no owner decision. P1's question 2 leaves out the board running from the DC input. In that state a host's VBUS (Voltage Bus) still faces the IO board's 5 V rail through the cable. P2 needs the answer to decide whether the display supply carries a reverse-blocking part (ideal diode or eFuse).
added.for_quantity: reverse-current blocking on the display supply

added.question: Which DC input current, in A, does R5 size the DC input's protection and the source selection for? Option 1: 4.9 A for the servo supply at 12 V, on the 90 % efficiency Power.md:68 assumes, plus the display, the encoder's 12 V supply and the logic rails. Option 2: the TPS55285's input current from its datasheet efficiency at 12 V in and 8.4 V, 6.35 A out ('for research'), plus the same loads.
added.why: Power.md:68 gives 90 % for the DC input with no source, and P1 marked no DC input current. At 12 V: 59.27 W / 12 V = 4.94 A for the servo supply. The display adds 7.5 W / 0.9 / 12 V = 0.69 A, making 5.63 A before the logic rails. That is above the TPS25947 seed's 5.5 A rating (www.ti.com/product/TPS25947, read 2026-09-28T10:33:19Z). Every series part on the DC input is rated from this figure.
added.for_quantity: DC input current at 90 % servo efficiency

added.question: In which order do the IO board's 5 V and 3.3 V rails come up at power-on and fall at power-off: 5 V first, 3.3 V first, or either order?
added.why: IOBoard.md:376 states that the order is not stated and assigns it to R5. The module build brings 3.3 V up after 5 V (STATUS.md:317-319). IOBoard.md:105 translates a 5 V output that drives before the 3.3 V rail is up. Research.md:270-272 require every front end on an ADC input to stay within rating while the 3.3 V rail is down. Without the order, P2 cannot choose between independent regulators and a sequenced pair (enable or power-good chaining).

added.question: With the 2S pack's power leads connected and its balance lead unplugged, or one balance wire open, does the disconnect hold the pack off: yes or no?
added.why: F9 reads the floor per cell from the balance lead (Research.md:537). Without the lead, no cell voltage reaches the disconnect. The tree's rule 'fail safe by absence' (CONTRIBUTING.md:34-35) is written for outputs, and no page states it for the pack. P2 cannot check whether a monitor detects an open balance wire, or whether the pack path defaults off, without the answer.
added.for_quantity: pack disconnect with the balance lead absent

added.question: At which current, in mA, is the encoder's supply output (5 V or 12 V, F4) limited, so that a short on the encoder cable leaves the 5 V rail and the display's supply in regulation? Answer 'none' if it has no limit.
added.why: The encoder's 5 V comes from the 5 V rail (IOBoard.md:338), which also feeds the display through the link cable. A display brown-out stops the heartbeat and opens every gate (docs/Safety.md:26-30). No page limits the current of a supply that leaves the board; IOBoard.md:536 states none even for shorted signal lines. P2 cannot decide whether the encoder output needs a current-limited switch without it.
